rules.statement: An owner who, through their own actions, prevents access to a road does not have a right of way of necessity over another's land.
rules.supporting_quote: (1) An owner of a land, who by his own act deprives himself of access to a road is not entitled to claim a right of way of necessity over the land of another. (2) When a piece of land is split into two or more parts, the back portion must retain its outlet over the front portion ever though nothing was said about it, because the splitting of the land cannot impose servitude upon the neighbours. 110 AN

rules.statement: A back portion of land retains an implied right to an outlet over a front portion after the land is split, even if no such arrangement was explicitly made.
